# Spiritual Translation: The Seven Works of Divine Wisdom and the Seven Evils of Falsity from Evil

---

**¶1:** The immensity of Divine Wisdom and its divinity: how was it formed after the likeness of the Divine Itself?

**¶2:** It is the entrance into spiritual life and the containing form of heavenly peace, belonging to this great heavenly state of wisdom [GAP-1: — the inmost heaven from which all illumination proceeds]. It is the passage through which the interiors of the spirit are liberated.

**¶4:** In every state of illumination, this great Divine Truth shining forth into the mind accomplishes seven full works of good for those who receive it.

**¶5:** The first good that it accomplishes is its wisdom, which it pours into the understanding. It opens the intellectual sight of all who are in the human state. They perceive the path of life as they walk by its guidance. It removes the ignorance of the state of spiritual darkness, which had closed their understanding with its falsity.

**¶6:** The second: When Divine Truth enters the mind, by its coming it brings heavenly tranquility and peace to the whole of the interior life. By its coming it also removes from them all the anxiety and dread with which their will was filled during the entire state of darkness; for it dispels the falsity that was present by means of its wisdom, and sweeps it away. And in this same manner it extinguishes spiritual fear by its peace.

**¶7:** The third is its awakening; because when Divine Truth enters the mind, all who were in spiritual torpor arise and become conscious. And the truths that had served as guardians during the state of obscurity are released from their vigilance. The protective truths stationed at the entrances of the ordered life — they cease their watch at the outposts of defense, because of the wisdom that has shone upon them within the mind.

**¶8:** The fourth: It nourishes, and gives power, interior perception of good, and perception of truth, to all perceptions and their works, and to all natural knowledges and every form of understanding, and to the first openings of spiritual thought, and to the most general natural truths, which exist upon the whole of the natural mind.

**¶9:** The fifth: When Divine Truth illumines the whole of the interior life, the evil lusts that creep in the lowest parts of the mind, and the predatory selfish affections that are filled with malice — they flee into concealment within their hidden interiors.

**¶10:** The sixth: When it shines its wisdom, the spiritual injury of any soul is eased of its suffering. Its truth dissolves the persuasions of falsity employed by every agent of evil.

**¶11:** The seventh: Divine Truth displays and makes manifest to the mind the sign of the glory of the heavenly states of wisdom, from which it has proceeded; it being, here within the natural mind, their representative. It brings illumination to the whole of what has been created in the spirit.

---

**¶13:** The state of spiritual darkness contains within itself all evils. In every instance when the state of falsity descends, it accomplishes seven evils within the mind.

**¶14:** The first evil that the state of spiritual darkness accomplishes in the mind is falsity, with which it fills the entire interior life; because when Divine Truth withdraws from the mind and gathers to itself its particular truths, at that instant the shadow of the state of ignorance spreads over the whole of the interior life. The understanding of the soul fills with obscurity. People neither perceive nor apprehend with their intellectual sight, because of the falsity from evil which fills the whole of the mind.

**¶15:** The second evil that the state of spiritual darkness accomplishes is its dread; because when its obscurity looms forth, its anxiety and its trembling take hold of all who are in the human state. The entire interior life fills with the darkness.

**¶16:** The third: When the state of falsity descends, all affections and thoughts take up rebellion. They turn in their will against Divine order, to commit evil and spiritual destruction.

**¶17:** The fourth: The heaviness of spiritual torpor lays upon them, and they fall into unconsciousness; they become insensible and stupefied, and they are like those who are spiritually dead in the state of darkness.

**¶18:** The fifth is its deformity; again, when the state of falsity descends, the spiritual form of the soul is hidden in the obscurity and the ugliness of that state. The beauty and the form of the celestial and the spiritual — the masculine understanding and the feminine will — are not displayed to one another, because of the falsity and the deformity which it spreads over all their forms.

**¶19:** The sixth occasion is when the state of spiritual darkness descends upon the mind. At that instant evil states of life come forth to do wickedness: the profaners of good, and the thieves of truth, and those who corrupt truth with falsity. The predatory evil affections come forth, and all the lusts that creep in the lowest parts of the mind, filled with malice, from their hidden interiors. And they prowl in the state of darkness. Also, the influences from hell and the infernal spirits find power to work evil in the state of falsity. Again, the assaults and violences and injuries and effusions of evil torment the soul in the darkness; because in it the whole of evil finds its strength.

**¶20:** The seventh: The state of spiritual darkness displays the sign of Evil itself, its origin. It has arisen out of the essence of evil; because this state of falsity that came forth from the primordial Evil has been displayed in the mind. Observe this state of spiritual darkness — it is the shadow of the primordial Evil, the one that is interwoven and bound into all things of the interior and the exterior life.

---

**¶22:** There are five essential qualities that manifest in Divine Wisdom, which it produces [GAP-2: — impressing them upon the interior forms of the mind] as it encounters the states of the world.

**¶23:** The first is its illumination; for it enlightens by its truth the whole of the mind, and all the affections and thoughts that exist within it.

**¶24:** The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it floods spiritual form and loveliness upon all affections and thoughts, and upon everything.

**¶25:** The third is its peace; for, again, when Divine Truth illumines the mind, all who are in the human state receive mutual love through it, and extend peace to one another.

**¶26:** The fourth is the liberation of the living spiritual essence, which it releases from all the bonds and constraints of what is interior and what is exterior.

**¶27:** The fifth: It gives power to the fundamental constituents of spiritual life; and also it gives perception of truth and interior perception of good to the whole of the Divine Life that is scattered and bound within natural forms.

**¶28:** Its wisdom illumines more than all lesser lights of understanding that exist in the mind. Also, its spiritual beauty is more beautiful than all the forms of merely human thought. Again, its peace surpasses all the powers and protections that exist in the mind. Its liberating power, by which it frees the living spiritual essence, is an entire state ahead of all other liberating actions! The strength that it gives to its members is a great strength, being mightier than all other powers!

---

**¶29:** Once again, there are another three essential qualities made apparent by Divine Wisdom, with respect to the mystery of the Divine Itself.

**¶30:** The first is the perpetual fullness of its containing form; because its vessel is filled in every state, and never diminishes at all, in the way that the containing form of faith from natural truth wanes and fluctuates. This unceasing fullness, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Divine Love, the infinite Divine Itself; from whom all the powers and the celestial beings have proceeded. He never diminishes, nor does any lack ever exist in Him!

**¶31:** The second: The wisdom of Divine Truth surpasses the light of all particular knowledges of good and truth, and all the illuminations that exist throughout the created universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Divine Love; for His wisdom surpasses and is greater than the illumination of all His heavenly societies.

**¶32:** The third: This Divine Wisdom is very high above all else. It surpasses the elevation of all the states of celestial love and spiritual love that exist upon the whole of the regenerate mind — corresponding to the mystery of the Divine Itself; for He is elevated above all the household of His heaven. Also, because the Divine Itself is exalted above all the elevations and the states of love within His heaven. He is perpetually full in His own image [GAP-3: through] all states and every moment from eternity to eternity!

---

**¶34:** The mystery of the first great illumination from the Divine is this Divine Wisdom, which is the derived light-bearer, the one that comes in every state of life into the mind. It displays all the marks of its Divine goods, manifesting and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the Good. It proceeded from the Divine Love and appeared within the natural mind.

**¶35:** This state of falsity that is constituted of dread exists after the pattern of Evil itself. Observe also the mystery of its essence! It displays itself in the mind through all these evils. It displays this mystery of its nature perpetually in the life of the world.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: the greatness of the sun and its divinity: how was it fashioned after the likeness of the first greatness?
it is the gate of life and the vessel of peace, to this great aeon of light [from which it came forth]. it is the gate of the souls' departure
Every day, would this great light-giver shine its light, it shall do seven good things for them.

The first good thing that it does for them is its light, which it shines upon them. It opens the eyes of all mankind. They see underfoot as they walk by it. It takes away the blindness of the night, which made them blind with its darkness.

The second: When (the sun) is come to the world, with its coming it shall bring calm and peace to the entire world. With its coming it shall also take away from them all the fear and trembling, which their heart is filled with the whole night; for it shall take away the darkness present by its light, and sweep it out. Also, this is how it extinguishes fear by its calm.

The third is its vigil; because when (the sun) comes to the world all sleeping mankind shall arise and awake. And the watchmen too shall cease from watching. The guards who sit at the gates of camps, they break vigil at the watchposts, because of its light that has shone upon them in the world.
The fourth: It shall nourish, and give strength, taste and scent, to the trees and fruits and vegetables, and all the herbs, and the flowers and grasses, which are upon the entire earth.
The fifth: When (the sun) shines in all the world, the evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts that are filled of wickedness, they shall flee to hiding in their dens.
The sixth: When it shines its light, the wound of any person is eased from pain. Its light shall melt away the evil arts of every doer of wickedness.

The seventh: (The sun) shall display and manifest to the world the sign of the splendour of the aeons of light, from which it has come out; it here in this world being their sign. It brings light to the whole of creation.
it has all wickednesses therein. Every occasion, would the night fall, it shall do seven evils in the world.

The first wickedness that the night shall do in the world is the darkness, with which it shall fill the entire world; because when the sun sinks from the world and draws to it its rays, at that instant the shadow of the night shall spread out over the whole world. The eyes of the people fill with blackness. They neither see nor wonder with their eyes, because of the darkness of the night which shall fill the whole world.
The second evil thing that the night shall do is its fear; because when its shadow looms forth, its fear and its trembling shall possess all of mankind. The entire world shall fill of the night.
The third: When the night falls, all creatures take up revolt. They rebel in their heart, to do wickedness and perdition.
The fourth: The heaviness of sleep shall lay upon them, and they fall asleep; they slumber and doze, and they are like these corpses in the night.

The fifth is its ugliness; again, when the night would fall, the form of the people shall be hidden in the darkness and the ugliness of the night. The beauty and the form of men and women shall not be displayed before one another, because of its darkness and its ugliness, which it shall spread out over all their forms.

The sixth occasion is when the night would fall on the world. At that instant evil people shall come out to do wickedness; the adulterers, and the robbers and poisoners. The evil beasts shall come out, and all the reptiles that are filled with wickedness, from their dens. And they stalk in the night. Also, the demons and fiends find power to do wickedness in the night. Again, the blows and buffets and wounds and discharges shall torment people in the night; because in it the whole of evil shall find strength.

The seventh: The night shall display the sign of the Darkness, its father. It has arisen out of its essence; because this night that came out of this first Darkness has been displayed in the world. Note this night, the shadow of this first Darkness, the one that is entwined and bound in all things above and below.
There are five archetypes occur in the sun, it making them [manifest to all] as it finds the world.
The first is its light; for it illumines by its light the world, and all the creatures who exist in it.
The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it shall flood beauty and loveliness upon all creatures and everything.
The third is its peace; for, again, when the sun would shine on the world, all people shall receive affection through it, and give peace to one another.
The fourth is the life of the living soul, which it shall release from all the bonds and fetters of heaven and earth.
The fifth: It gives a strength to the elements; and also it gives a scent and a taste to the entire Cross of the Light.

its light illumines more than all lights that occur in the world. Also, its beauty is more beautiful than all the beauties of mankind. Again, its peace is more surpassing than all the powers and guards who exist in the world. Its releasing action, by which it releases the living soul, is a full day ahead of all releasing actions! The strength that it gives to its limbs is a great strength, being mightier than all strengths!
Once again, there are another three archetypes made apparent by the sun, in respect of the mystery of the first greatness.

The first is the filling up of the disk of its ship; because its ship has filled up every season, and shall not wane at all, the way that the ship of the moon wanes. This continuous filling, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Father, the great greatness; from whom all the powers and the gods have come forth. He shall never wane, nor shall lack ever exist in him!

The second: (The sun's) light surpasses the light of all the stars, and all the lights that occur in the universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Father; for his light surpasses and is greater than the light of his aeons.

The third: This sun is very high above all else. It surpasses the height of all the mountains and hills that exist upon the entire earth, corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness; for he is high above all the household of his light-earth. Also, because the Father himself is high above all the heights and the mountains of his light-earth. He is 'filled up' in his image [all] the time and every hour from eternity to eternity!

The mystery of the first great light is the sun, which is this second light-giver, the one that comes daily to the world. It displays all the marks of its graces, displaying and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the good. It came from the good Father and appeared in this world.

this night that is made of fear exists after the mystery of the Darkness. Behold too the mystery of its essence! It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses. It displays this mystery daily in the world.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading indicates "the inmost heaven from which all illumination proceeds," and the Kephalaia's own register repeatedly uses the phrase "from which it has come out" (¶11) and "from whom all the powers... have come forth" (¶30) to describe the sun's origin in the great aeon of light.

The spiritual reading says "impressing them upon the interior forms of the mind," which in the Kephalaia's natural register means the sun makes its archetypes manifest/apparent to all creatures when it encounters the world; the parallel phrase in ¶29 ("made apparent by the sun") confirms this vocabulary.

The editor's "all" is confirmed: "all the time and every hour" forms a natural parallel doublet expressing perpetual fullness, matching the Kephalaia's characteristic style of doubling temporal expressions, and corresponds to the spiritual sense of the Divine being perpetually full throughout all states.
